name: container
description: Centered max-width wrapper that constrains content to readable widths. Sizes map to `--container-*` prose-width tokens; padding maps to `--space-*`.

props.name: size
props.description: Max-width preset bound to `--container-*` tokens (sm=33rem, md=40rem, lg=50rem, xl=66rem, full=100%).

props.name: padding
props.description: Horizontal padding bound to `--space-*` tokens (none=0, sm=0.75rem, md=1rem, lg=2rem).

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render as a different element via Radix `Slot`. Use to render as `<main>`, `<section>`, etc. for landmark semantics.

values.description: 66rem (≈1056px) — wider canvas for dashboards or marketing.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Page content to constrain — typically a section, article, or grid.

examples.title: Reading-width article
examples.description: lg size (50rem) + md padding for an article body.

examples.title: Full-width hero
examples.description: Use size=full when you want the section to span the viewport.

ai.whenToUse: Use to constrain page content to readable widths. Pair with `Stack` or `Grid` inside for vertical/grid layouts. Default for any centered article, settings page, or marketing section.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use inside another `Container` (double-clamping). Don't use as a drop-in for `<main>` semantics — it's a layout primitive, not a landmark. For full-bleed sections (edge-to-edge banners), pass `size="full" padding="none"`.
commonMistakes: Wrapping a `Container` in another `Container` and getting an unexpectedly narrow column
Using `padding="none"` and forgetting that children still need their own gutter — the parent contributes nothing
Treating `lg` as the largest size — `xl` (66rem) and `full` are bigger
ai.accessibilityNotes: Container is presentational. Wrap in a semantic landmark (`<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`) when the page structure needs it; Container itself renders a plain `<div>`.
